q: Under Sec. 11.3.2 of SPP Doc. 206, if the Architect acting as Project Manager also performs Regular Design Services for the same project, how is he/she compensated for the design services?
o: Separately, as stipulated under SPP Doc. 202
Through a deduction from the Construction Manager's fee
No additional compensation; design services are already included in the 2%-5% Project Manager fee
Only through an informally negotiated Lump Sum fee outside the SPP
n: Sec. 11.3.2 provides that if the Architect as Project Manager performs Regular Design Services for the same project, he/she is compensated separately for these services as stipulated in SPP Doc. 202. (Source: SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.3.2)

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four methods of compensation listed under SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.2, for the Architect acting as Project Manager?
o: Lump Sum or Fixed Fee
Percentage of Project Construction Cost
Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense
Per Diem, Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses
n: Sec. 11.2 lists only four methods for Comprehensive Architectural Services: Percentage of PCC, Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense, Professional Fee plus Expenses, and Lump Sum or Fixed Fee. "Per Diem, Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses" is instead a method used under Construction Management Services (Sec. 9) and Design-Build Services (Sec. 12). (Source: SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.2.1-11.2.4)

q: An Architect performing Comprehensive Architectural Services was paid ₱1,050,000 as professional fee for a project with a Project Construction Cost of ₱30,000,000. Is this fee within the SPP Doc. 206 recommended range?
o: No, it is below the recommended minimum of 2%
Yes, it is exactly 3.5% of PCC, which falls within the 2%-5% range
No, it exceeds the recommended maximum of 5%
It cannot be determined without knowing the Direct Personnel Expense
n: ₱1,050,000 ÷ ₱30,000,000 = 0.035 = 3.5% of PCC, which lies between the 2% floor and 5% ceiling recommended under Sec. 11.3.1. (Source: SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.3.1)

q: Under Sec. 11.1.3 of SPP Doc. 206, if the Owner directly hires a Project Manager, whose responsibility is it to hire the Construction Manager?
o: The Project Manager
The Owner alone, without any involvement of the Project Manager
The Architect-of-Record
The Full-Time Construction Supervisor
n: Sec. 11.1.3 states that if a Project Manager is hired by the Owner, it is the responsibility of the Project Manager to hire the Construction Manager, who may be paid by the Project Manager or by the Owner on a salary or percentage-of-construction-cost basis. (Source: SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.1.3)

q: How many categories of experts are enumerated in SPP Doc. 206 as possible members of the Architect's professional team under Comprehensive Architectural Services?
n: The team enumerated is: Architects, Engineers, Market Analyst, Accountants, General Contractors, Real Estate Consultants, Sociologists, Planners, Bankers, and Lawyers — ten categories in total. (Source: SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.1.2.1-11.1.2.10)

q: What is the full range (low to high) of the recommended professional fee for this project under Sec. 11.3.1?
n: At 2% and 5% of the ₱20,000,000 PCC, the recommended fee ranges from ₱400,000 (2%) to ₱1,000,000 (5%). (Source: SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.3.1)
scenario: A Client engages an Architect to render Comprehensive Architectural Services (acting as Project Manager) for a project with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of ₱20,000,000.

q: Under SPP Doc. 206, the Architect performing Comprehensive Architectural Services may expand his/her staff by hiring experts to form a professional team. Which of the following is explicitly listed as part of this professional team?
o: Market Analysts
Politicians
Insurance Underwriters
Advertising Executives
n: The enumerated professional team includes Architects, Engineers, Market Analyst, Accountants, General Contractors, Real Estate Consultants, Sociologists, Planners, Bankers, and Lawyers. Market Analysts are on this list; the other choices are not. (Source: SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.1 (11.1.2.1-11.1.2.10))

scenario: A Client engages an Architect to render Comprehensive Architectural Services (acting as Project Manager) for a project with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of ₱20,000,000.

q: An Architect is engaged as Project Manager for Comprehensive Architectural Services and is also asked to prepare the actual architectural design (from schematic design through construction documents) for the same project. According to SPP Doc. 206, what should the Architect do regarding fees?
o: Charge only the Design-Build rate of 7% of PCC for all work combined
Charge a separate, additional fee for the Regular Design Services under SPP Doc. 202, on top of the Project Manager compensation
Decline to do the design work since it conflicts with the Project Manager role
Absorb the design work within the 2%-5% Project Manager fee since it is part of "comprehensive" services
n: Per Sec. 11.3.2, Regular Design Services rendered by the Architect-as-Project-Manager on the same project are compensated separately under SPP Doc. 202, in addition to the 2%-5% Project Manager fee under Sec. 11.3.1. (Source: SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.3.2)

q: Which set correctly lists the four methods of compensation for the Architect performing Comprehensive Architectural Services (as Project Manager) under SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.2?
o: Percentage of PCC; Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense; Per Diem, Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses; Mixed Methods of Compensation
Percentage of PCC; Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense; Professional Fee plus Expenses; Lump Sum or Fixed Fee
Value-pricing; Monthly salary/fee; Retainer plus Reimbursable Expenses; Professional Fee plus Expenses
Percentage of PCC; Mixed Methods of Compensation; Built-in in the Guaranteed Maximum Cost; Retainer
n: Sec. 11.2.1 to 11.2.4 lists exactly: Percentage of Project Construction Cost, Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense, Professional Fee plus Expenses, and Lump Sum or Fixed Fee. (Source: SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.2)

q: An Architect performing Comprehensive Architectural Services was paid ₱2,400,000 as professional fee for a project with a Project Construction Cost of ₱40,000,000. Is this fee within the SPP Doc. 206 recommended range?
o: No, 6% is below the recommended minimum of 2%
No, 6% exceeds the recommended maximum of 5%
Yes, 6% is within the recommended range
Yes, because Comprehensive Architectural Services have no fee ceiling
n: ₱2,400,000 ÷ ₱40,000,000 = 0.06 = 6% of PCC, which exceeds the 5% ceiling recommended under Sec. 11.3.1. (Source: SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.3.1)

q: In Comprehensive Architectural Services, the Full-Time Construction Supervisor, per SPP Doc. 206, will be:
o: Always a subcontractor's employee, never connected to the Project Manager or Owner
Either with the staff of the Project Manager or hired directly by the Owner
Prohibited from ever being part of the Project Manager's staff
Always paid a percentage of the Architect's design fee only
n: Sec. 11.1.3 provides that, in the same manner as the Construction Manager, the Full-Time Construction Supervisor will either be with the staff of the Project Manager or hired by the Owner. (Source: SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.1.3)

q: For a project with a Project Construction Cost of ₱8,000,000, what is the difference between the HIGH-END and LOW-END recommended professional fees under SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.3.1?
n: Low-end (2%) = ₱160,000; high-end (5%) = ₱400,000. The difference is ₱400,000 − ₱160,000 = ₱240,000 (equivalent to the 3-percentage-point spread × ₱8,000,000). (Source: SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.3.1)

q: A Client wants to develop a large mixed-use complex and needs one entity to coordinate design, financing feasibility, market studies, legal matters, and construction procurement, in addition to architectural design. Under the SPP, which service arrangement should the Architect propose?
o: Post-Construction Services under SPP Doc. 205
Construction Management Services under SPP Doc. 204-B only
Regular Design Services under SPP Doc. 202 only
Comprehensive Architectural Services under SPP Doc. 206
n: Comprehensive Architectural Services under SPP Doc. 206 is precisely the arrangement where the Architect acts as Project Manager/overall coordinator and expands the team with market analysts, real estate consultants, lawyers, bankers, and other experts to cover the full scope described. (Source: SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.1)

q: What is the primary characteristic of Comprehensive Architectural Services under SPP Doc. 206, distinguishing it from the Architect's regular design services?
o: The Architect assumes the role of Project Manager, Project Development Manager, or overall coordinator for the project, in addition to design
The Architect acts strictly as a building administrator managing rental collections
The Architect performs only construction supervision after project completion
The Architect solely audits contractor invoices
n: Under Sec. 11.1, the Architect normally enters into a contract with the Owner to perform comprehensive architectural services; by the very nature of these services, he/she assumes the role of Project Manager, Project Development Manager, or overall coordinator. (Source: SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.1)

q: What is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for the Architect acting as Project Manager under SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.3.1?
o: 2% to 5% of the Project Construction Cost
7% of the Project Construction Cost
1.5% to 3% of the Project Construction Cost
4% to 6% of gross rental
n: Sec. 11.3.1 recommends a fee of 2% to 5% of the Project Construction Cost (PCC) for the Architect acting as Project Manager under Comprehensive Architectural Services. (The other figures belong to different SPP documents: 1.5%-3% is the Construction Manager's fee under Sec. 9, 4%-6% of gross rental is the Post-Construction Services fee under Sec. 10, and 7% of PCC is the Design-Build-by-Administration fee under Sec. 12.) (Source: SPP Doc. 206, Sec. 11.3.1)
